question: In which year was Mendeleev’s Periodic Table published in a German journal?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1872**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chemist and inventor Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev was from Russia. His most famous works are the Periodic Law and a modified periodic chart of elements. The first periodic table was created by Mendeleev, and printed in 1869.
 
• In order to represent similarities and patterns in the behaviour of elements, Mendeleev created the periodic table, which is an arrangement of elements in an increasing atomic mass order in tablet form.
 
• In the periodic table, the elements were arranged into 7 Horizontal rows in ascending order of atomic known as periods and 8 vertices column known as groups.
 
• When two elements are highly similar to one another, the new element is positioned immediately below the older element that shares the same characteristic to begin a new period. Lithium, potassium, rubidium, and other first-group elements are some examples.
 
• One period below the other creates a "column" (group). Thus, the horizontal rows and vertical columns, or the periods and groups, respectively, make up Mendeleev's periodic table.
 
• If two elements are similar but not by much, they are separated by being placed below but somewhat distant from one other. Each column will contain two sub-columns (A and B), allowing for more similarity between entries inside each sub-column.
 
• Transitional elements are categorised into group VIII, while normal elements are divided into groups I through VII.
 
• Group VIII consists of three parts, while Groups I through VII is split into two subgroups.
 
• The first series and the second series are separated into the fourth through seventh grades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Difference between the Modern periodic table and Mendeleev's periodic table -

 
 

 **Mendeleev's periodic table **
 **Modern periodic table ** 
 
 

 
 
Atomic mass is the foundation of Mendeleev's periodic table.

 
 The atomic number is the foundation of the current periodic table.
 
 

 Around 63 elements can be found in Mendeleev's periodic table.
 There are approximately 118 elements in the current periodic table.
 
 

 Mendeleev's periodic chart contained gaps for elements that had not yet been identified
 The periodic table of today keeps its homogeneity.
 
 

 Noble gases were not included in Mendeleev's periodic chart (as they are not discovered at that time).
 Group 18 on the modern periodic table is a separate category for noble gases. 
 
 

 Transitional elements are listed with other elements in Mendeleev's periodic table
 Transitional elements are arranged in a separate blocks in the modern periodic table.
